alt.en: The top of a printed music page, numbered 164, with the title "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel" in black-letter type, the word "Chorus" and one staff of music in four flats and 2/4 time.
alt.es: La parte superior de una página de música impresa, con el número 164, el título "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel" en letra gótica, la palabra "Chorus" y un pentagrama con cuatro bemoles y en 2/4.

caption.en: The head of page 164 of Hampton Institute's 1909 songbook, this song's earliest known printing: its black-letter title over the refrain, headed "Chorus", in A-flat major and 2/4 time.
caption.es: La parte superior de la página 164 del cancionero del Hampton Institute de 1909, la primera impresión conocida de esta canción: su título en letra gótica sobre el estribillo, con el encabezado "Chorus" (coro), en La bemol mayor y en 2/4.

source: Religious Folk Songs of the Negro as Sung on the Plantations, new edition, arranged by the musical directors of the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute (Hampton, Va.: The Institute Press, 1909), p. 164, "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel"; top of the page (the title, "Chorus" and the first treble staff only, cut above the words)
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M1670 .H3 R4 MUSI; OCLC 977588305; Internet Archive religiousfolkson00hamp, image n173
licenceEvidence: "Copyright, July 1, 1909", Hampton, Va.: US works published before 1931 are public domain. Arranged by the institute's unnamed musical directors; the song is anonymous and traditional; 70 years from 1909 ended in 1979 in the EU and Israel. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of a printed music page, numbered 60, headed "Hymns on Biblical Themes" and "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel", marked "Poco allegro ritmo marcato", a quarter note equal to 90, "Refrain", "Tutti" and mf, over one staff of music in four flats and 2/4 time.
alt.es: La parte superior de una página de música impresa, con el número 60 y los encabezados "Hymns on Biblical Themes" y "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel", con las indicaciones "Poco allegro ritmo marcato", negra igual a 90, "Refrain", "Tutti" y mf, sobre un pentagrama con cuatro bemoles y en 2/4.

caption.en: Page 60 of R. Nathaniel Dett's Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), which reprints the 1909 setting and adds a tempo, a quarter note at 90, and marks the refrain "Tutti", for everyone.
caption.es: La página 60 de Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), de R. Nathaniel Dett, que reimprime la armonización de 1909 y le añade un tempo, negra a 90, y marca el estribillo "Tutti", para todos.

source: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton, Va.: Hampton Institute Press, 1927), "Hymns on Biblical Themes", "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel", p. 60; top of the page (headings, markings and the first treble staff only)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: BV461 .R477 1927; Internet Archive religiousfolkson00dett, image n91
licenceEvidence: Copyright 1927 by the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute: US works published in 1927 entered the public domain on 1 January 2023; Dett died 1943, so life plus 70 ended on 1 January 2014 in the EU and Israel. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A black and white photograph of a large Victorian building with a steep slate roof lined with dormer windows and a pointed tower at the left corner, seen through bare winter trees across a lawn. A long porch runs along the ground floor, a plainer brick wing stands at the right, and the caption "Virginia and Cleveland Halls" is printed below.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un gran edificio victoriano con un empinado tejado de pizarra lleno de buhardillas y una torre puntiaguda en la esquina izquierda, visto entre árboles desnudos de invierno al otro lado de un césped. Un largo porche recorre la planta baja, a la derecha hay un ala de ladrillo más sencilla y debajo está impreso el pie "Virginia and Cleveland Halls".

caption.en: Virginia and Cleveland Halls at Hampton Institute in Virginia, in the school's own catalogue of about 1901. Hampton's songbook of 1909 is the earliest known printing of Ezekiel Saw the Wheel; its students had sung and published spirituals since the 1870s.
caption.es: Virginia Hall y Cleveland Hall en el Instituto Hampton, en Virginia, en el catálogo de la propia escuela de hacia 1901. El cancionero de Hampton de 1909 es la primera impresión conocida de Ezekiel Saw the Wheel; sus estudiantes cantaban y publicaban espirituales desde la década de 1870.

source: "Virginia and Cleveland Halls", photograph in the Catalogue of the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute (Hampton: Institute Steam Press), bound volume of catalogues 1896 to 1903, next to the catalogue for 1900 to 1901
library: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (digitized by the Internet Archive; Internet Archive Book Images on Flickr, via Wikimedia Commons)
